item.title: 🌟 On November 26, the Victory Museum opened the exhibition Marshal of Victory: 130 Years
item.description: 🌟 On November 26, the Victory Museum opened the exhibition Marshal of Victory: 130 Years , marking the 130th anniversary of the birth of Georgy Zhukov . The exhibition features authentic historical artefacts from the family archives of the Marshal’s descendants, as well as items and documents from the collections of the Victory Museum, members of the Association of Historical and Military History Museums , and the country’s largest archives. For the first time in Moscow, visitors will be able to see the first-ever Order of Victory , awarded to Georgy Zhukov in the spring of 1944 for the liberation of Right-Bank Ukraine in the Ukrainian SSR . Also on November 26, the Victory Museum launched the International Open Forum Zhukov: Legacy , the centrepiece of the celebrations marking the 130th anniversary of the legendary military commander’s birth . On November 27, an international academic conference dedicated to the Marshal’s anniversary will open as part of the forum. It will bring together Russian and foreign historians, representatives of research institutions, archives and museums, educators, government officials, representatives of public organisations, university students and schoolchildren. The event was organised with the involvement of the Military History Institute of the Military Academy of the General Staff of the Russian Armed Forces, the Russian Historical Society , the Russian Military Historical Society , the Russian Foreign Ministry and Rossotrudnichestvo . item.title: 🗓 On November 26, the Cultural Centre of the Foreign Ministry’s Main Administration for Servicing the Diplomatic Corps (GlavUpDK)
item.description: 🗓 On November 26, the Cultural Centre of the Foreign Ministry’s Main Administration for Servicing the Diplomatic Corps (GlavUpDK) hosted a presentation of the investment, economic and tourism potential of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra , attended by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov , Governor of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra Ruslan Kukharuk and representatives of the diplomatic corps, the business community, and Russian and foreign media. In his remarks, Sergey Lavrov highlighted the achievements of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra and the experience it has gained through its active engagement with foreign partners , particularly in the extraction and supply of energy resources and in tourism . He made special mention of the rich cultural and historical heritage of this constituent entity of the Russian Federation. During the event, those present were introduced to the Area’s natural diversity and distinctive traditions , its unique experience in preserving the way of life of the indigenous peoples of the North and the projects under way in the region, including in digital technologies . The participants expressed confidence that the presentation would provide further impetus for deepening cooperation and diversifying the international ties of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra, above all with friendly countries , in the economic, educational, scientific and cultural spheres.

🎙
Foreign Minister
Sergey Lavrov’s
opening remarks
at the presentation of the
Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area
(Moscow, November 26, 2026)
💬
Mr Kukharuk, Ladies and gentlemen, colleagues and friends,
I am delighted to welcome you to the presentation of the
Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra
, a distinctive region of the Russian Federation about which you have just been given a brief but, to my mind, highly vivid account. I am convinced that the remainder of the presentation will spark even greater interest among you.
Unfortunately, I have visited Khanty-Mansiysk only once. That was long ago, in 2007, when I took part in the
Conference on the Development of International Regional Ties of the Constituent Entities of the Russian Federation
and attended the opening of the local branch of the Russian Commission for UNESCO there. Almost 20 years have passed, and today it is particularly gratifying for me to highlight the successes achieved by this region of the Russian Federation.
☝️
It is an industrially developed area with immense economic, investment and tourism potential
and a most interesting history, culture and traditions. Today, I promised Governor of the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Area – Yugra Ruslan
Ruslan Kukharuk
that I would certainly visit next year, all the more so as there will be great reasons to come back. We will certainly follow through – we will continue our close cooperation.
The diversification of the regional economy and the creation of an innovative economic architecture, driven by the leadership of Yugra, make it possible to achieve a
synergistic effect
from the harmonious combination of vast mineral resources, modern technologies, and high-quality human capital. As a result, the Khanty-Mansi Area
occupies a prominent place
among the regions with a high share of exports and among the leading contributors to the federal budget. <...>
Yugra’s unique experience in preserving the culture and traditional way of life of the
indigenous peoples of the North – the Khanty, Mansi and Nenets
– as well as its efforts to preserve biodiversity, which is so vital for our planet now, deserves particular attention. Representatives of the region’s indigenous peoples are traditionally involved in the work of Russian delegations at specialised UN fora in
New York, Geneva and Nairobi
.
<...>
🤝
On the instructions of President
Vladimir Putin
, an International Friendship Club has been established in the region, bringing together participants from
44 foreign countries
. Moreover, the Club’s key project – the International Arctic Volunteer Corps – has been included in the national Action Plan for the International Year of Volunteers for Sustainable Development.
At the end of last year, the Khanty-Mansi Area
ranked first among Russian regions in volunteer activity
, charity and the non-profit sector, and second in the national rating for the effectiveness of youth policy implementation. All this is in addition to the leading positions the Area occupies in the economy.
I strongly believe that today’s presentation will not only provide an account of Yugra’s achievements but
will also serve as a starting point
for new, interesting and promising joint initiatives involving partners from the countries represented here.
I have no doubt that you will recognise the true worth of the advantages and opportunities Yugra offers and will report on them to your governments and economic operators. Our
ministry
will do everything it can to help establish ties and advance promising, mutually beneficial projects.

item.title: 📺 #Opinion BESOGON (Nikita Mikhalkov's programme) Europeans are now choosing those who could represent them in peace negotiations.
item.description: #Opinion 📺 BESOGON (Nikita Mikhalkov's programme) : Europeans are now choosing those who could represent them in peace negotiations. But there is no one to choose from. Perhaps for the first time in the centuries-long history of international relations, a field where every word is carefully weighed has been so heavily populated by people distinguished by their unrestrained rudeness and verbal intemperance. 👉 This, of course, is no coincidence. This process of negative selection is fuelled by Europe's military-industrial complex, driven mad by greed and in cahoots with those who frighten their populations with the alleged Russian threat and pocket kickbacks from new arms contracts, all while fuelling and sustaining anti-Russian hysteria. There are only two possible ways forward: either take Russia's outstretched hand or go to war against it, failing to understand that, for all the suffering this terrible war may inflict on our country, Europe itself would disappear from the map of the world. November 16, 2026

#RussiaWithAfrica
Food security beyond supply: Why Africa and the Global South need fairer agricultural markets
✍️
An article by Russian Ambassador to South Africa and Lesotho
Roman Ambarov,
published in
Independent Online (IOL),
The Public Eye
and
Lesotho Tribune
newspapers.
Key takeaways:
Russia: A reliable partner in ensuring food security
🔴
Russia remains
a reliable agricultural partner for Africa,
supplying
over 18 million tonnes
of grain in 2025 and a further
13 million tonnes
in the first nine months of 2026.
🔴
Russian fertiliser exports to Africa
exceeded 2.2 million tonnes
in 2026, helping support agricultural production across the continent.
🔴
Africa has
enormous agricultural potential.
Investment in irrigation, mechanisation, infrastructure, modern technologies and local processing can help the continent
reduce import dependence and become a major agricultural exporter.
🔴
Russia is ready to share its expertise and technologies
in agricultural machinery, seed production, fertilisers, livestock farming, storage, processing and logistics.
🔴
Russia's approach is based on partnership, not dependency
– combining Africa's agricultural resources and development priorities with Russian technological expertise and production capabilities.
Protecting the routes that feed the world
🔴
With Western backing, Kiev has
intensified attacks on Russian civilian vessels
,
grain terminals and agricultural export infrastructure
in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. August drone strikes on Novorossiysk grain terminals temporarily disrupted facilities with a combined annual capacity of
15.6 million tonnes.
🔴
Russia is adapting its export logistics. The development of
alternative transport corridors, including Arctic routes
, helps maintain the continuity of agricultural exports despite external pressures.
Who determines the price of food?
🔴
Russia is
a major global grain supplier
. It exported approximately
53 million tonnes of grain
in 2024/25, including
44 million tonnes of wheat
, to more than 100 countries, with grain export potential of at least
60 million tonnes.
🔴
Global agricultural prices are largely shaped by Western financial centres.
CBOT, Euronext and ICE play a major role in price formation, raising questions about the fairness and representativeness of the current system.
🔴
The Global South needs a greater voice in agricultural pricing.
It is in the interests of the Global South to develop more representative agricultural trading infrastructure and strengthen its participation in international price formation.
Russia proposes a BRICS Grain Exchange
The initiative aims to give major grain-producing countries a greater role in setting fair, predictable agricultural prices.
🔴
The initiative is gaining momentum. Supported by the
2024 Kazan Declaration
, the proposal advanced in 2026, with the BRICS New Delhi Declaration reaffirming the need to develop the platform and refine its operational modalities.
🔴
Russia-Africa cooperation
should go beyond supplies
to include technology transfer, investment, local processing and strengthening agricultural sovereignty, ensuring African countries become market-shapers rather than price-takers.

🎙
Remarks
by Russia's Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at a meeting with participants in the Dialogue for the Future programme organised by
the Alexander Gorchakov Public Diplomacy Fund
(Moscow, November 26, 2026)
Key points
:
•
The old order
that has prevailed for 500 years – dominated first by Europe and later by the “collective West” –
is inevitably giving way to new centres of growth
. This is not the result of revolutions, but
a natural historical process
driven by the laws of socioeconomic development.
• We have pursued a consistent policy.
We have never tried to impose anything on anyone.
We have always advocated, firstly,
collective consideration of problems
, whether at the
#UN
, the
#OSCE
or any other forum, and, secondly,
honouring the agreements reached
. Words must match deeds.
•
We were deceived time and again in the early years following the dissolution of the Soviet Union
, when Russia was assuming an independent role on the international stage and reaching agreements with the Americans and Europeans.
The NATO-Russia Council
was established, and an extensive framework of relations between Russia and the EU was developed. Yet all of this was brought down overnight simply because it was decided that
Russia had no right to defend its legitimate interests.
• Had it not been for Ukraine, another pretext would have been found to evade commitments to equal and mutually beneficial cooperation.
☝️
All the West ever wanted was to dictate its terms.
• Since President
Donald Trump
took office, the US has demonstrated
a degree of political maturity
that has long been absent in Europe. Despite the remaining differences, the Americans are
open to dialogue
and, moreover, are interested in maintaining diplomatic and other contacts.
• No two countries on Earth can have interests that coincide 100% on every issue, especially when it comes to major powers such as the US and Russia. This was true both during the Cold War and in the era of détente.
Dialogue, however, is essential under all circumstances.
To their credit, the Americans understand this and are
engaging in dialogue
on Ukraine, recognising
the need to eliminate the root causes of the crisis
, namely the creation of threats to Russia’s security right on our borders.
•
We are a people accustomed to facing all manner of trials.
Our people have endured them in the past, are enduring them now and will undoubtedly continue to do so in the future. At the same time,
we remain open to dialogue with everyone
, but it must be a dialogue between decent people, conducted in a manner befitting decent people.
